32191-the-sentimental-vikings.creator: Unknown
32191-the-sentimental-vikings.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. my lady’s chambers, a long, low wail of a child, strong and insistent, and then a man’s tread for a few paces, and then silence again, save for the men’s whisperings and the sound of the squeaking of their leather-belts as they moved, and the gentle rubbing of the wooden shields on the walls as the wind blew through under the rafters.

arxiv-2012-12638.title: On non-adaptive majority problems of large query size
arxiv-2012-12638.creator: Dániel Gerbner, Máté Vizer
arxiv-2012-12638.description: Abstract We are given n n balls and an unknown coloring of them with two colors. Our goal is to find a ball that belongs to the larger color class, or show that the color classes have the same size.

arxiv-2109-00603.title: Are stripped envelope supernovae really deficient in 56 Ni? Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2109-00603.creator: Ryoma Ouchi, Keiichi Maeda, Joseph P. Anderson, Ryo Sawada
arxiv-2109-00603.description: Abstract Recent works have indicated that the 56 Ni masses estimated for Stripped Envelope SNe (SESNe) are systematically higher than those estimated for SNe II. Although this may suggest a distinct progenitor structure between these types of SNe, the possibility remains that this may be caused by observational bias.

arxiv-2109-08997.title: The Modular Stone-von Neumann Theorem
arxiv-2109-08997.creator: Lucas Hall, Leonard Huang, John Quigg
arxiv-2109-08997.description: Abstract . In this paper, we use the tools of nonabelian duality to formulate and prove a far-reaching generalization of the Stone-von Neumann Theorem to modular representations of actions and coactions of locally compact groups on elementary C ∗ C^{\ast} -algebras. This greatly extends the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem for Actions of Abelian Groups recently proven by L.

arxiv-2202-02861.title: New Time-Resolved, Multi-Band Flares In The GJ 65 System With gPhoton Journal: ApJ Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , gPhoton ( Million et al. 2016 )
arxiv-2202-02861.creator: Scott W. Fleming, Chase Million, Rachel A. Osten, Dmitrii Y. Kolotkov, C. E. Brasseur
arxiv-2202-02861.description: Abstract Characterizing the distribution of flare properties and occurrence rates is important for understanding habitability of M dwarf exoplanets. The GALEX space telescope observed the GJ 65 system, composed of the active, flaring M stars BL Cet and UV Cet, for 15900 seconds ( ∼ \sim 4.4 hours) in two ultraviolet bands.

arxiv-2212-07340.title: Observational constraints on cosmic-ray escape from ultra-high energy accelerators
arxiv-2212-07340.creator: Olivier Deligny
arxiv-2212-07340.description: Abstract The energy spectrum and mass composition of ultra-high energy cosmic rays inferred at the Pierre Auger Observatory are used to derive a benchmark scenario for the emission mechanisms at play in extragalactic accelerators as well as for their energetics and for the abundances of elements in their environments.

arxiv-2303-00399.title: D4FT: A Deep Learning Approach to Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory Thanks: Equal Contribution. Our code will be available on https://github.com/sail-sg/d4ft .
arxiv-2303-00399.creator: Tianbo Li, Min Lin, Zheyuan Hu, Kunhao Zheng, Giovanni Vignale, Kenji Kawaguchi, A. H. Castro Neto, Kostya S. Novoselov, Shuicheng Yan
arxiv-2303-00399.description: Abstract Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (KS-DFT) has been traditionally solved by the Self-Consistent Field (SCF) method. Behind the SCF loop is the physics intuition of solving a system of non-interactive single-electron wave functions under an effective potential. In this work, we propose a deep learning approach to KS-DFT.

arxiv-2402-16754.title: Ambiguity Function Shaping in FMCW Automotive Radar Thanks: * First two authors have equal contributions.
arxiv-2402-16754.creator: Zahra Esmaeilbeig ∗1⋄ , Arindam Bose ∗2† , Mojtaba Soltanalian 3⋄
arxiv-2402-16754.description: Abstract Frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar with inter-chirp coding produces high side-lobes in the Doppler and range dimensions of the radar’s ambiguity function. The high side-lobes may cause miss-detection due to masking between targets that are at similar range and have large received power difference, as is often the case in automotive scenarios.

arxiv-2412-20190.title: Maximizing Predictive Performance for Small Subgroups: Functionally Adaptive Interaction Regularization (FAIR)
arxiv-2412-20190.creator: Daniel Smolyak, Courtney Paulson, Margrét V. Bjarnadóttir
arxiv-2412-20190.description: Abstract In many healthcare settings, it is both critical to consider fairness when building analytical applications but also uniquely unacceptable to lower model performance for one group to match that of another (e.g. fairness cannot be achieved by lowering the diagnostic ability of a model for one group to match that of another and lose overall diagnostic power).

arxiv-2504-00880.title: Group Accretion in Milky Way-like Stellar Haloes
arxiv-2504-00880.creator: Thomas M. Callingham, Amina Helmi
arxiv-2504-00880.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas M. Callingham, Amina Helmi. As galaxies form hierarchically, larger satellites may accrete alongside smaller companions in group infall events. This coordinated accretion is likely to have left signatures in the Milky Way’s stellar halo at the present day. Our goal is to characterise the possible groups of companions that accompanied larger known accretion events of our Galaxy, and infer where their stellar material could be in physical and dynamical space at present day.

arxiv-2506-10906.title: Analytic model for neutral penetration and plasma fueling
arxiv-2506-10906.creator: George J. Wilkie
arxiv-2506-10906.description: Abstract Neutral atoms recycled from wall interaction interact with confined plasma, thereby refueling it, most strongly in the region closest to the wall. This occurs near the X-point in diverted configurations, or else near the wall itself in limited configurations.

arxiv-2606-11069.creator: Yuchen Ding, Huixi Li, Junfeng Li, Wei Niu and Xiamiao Zhao

europmc-pmc5297507.creator: Gheith O, Farouk N, Nampoory N, Halim MA, Al-Otaibi T.
europmc-pmc5297507.description: Diabetic kidney disease - which is defined by elevated urine albumin excretion or reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR) or both - is a serious complication that occurs in 20% to 40% of all diabetics. In this review we try to highlight the prevalence of diabetic nephropathy...

pmc-10609817.title: Root Development Monitoring under Different Water Supply Levels in Processing Tomato Plants
pmc-10609817.creator: Oussama M’hamdi, Márton Égei, Zoltán Pék, Riadh Ilahy, Eszter Nemeskéri, Lajos Helyes, Sándor Takács, Hongbo Shao
pmc-10609817.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Managing crop yields and optimizing water use is a global challenge, as fresh water supply decreases rapidly and demand remains high. Therefore, understanding how plants react to varying water levels is crucial for efficient water usage. This study evaluates how tomato plants adapt to varying water levels (100%, 50% of crop evapotranspiration, and non-irrigated control) over two growing seasons in 2020 and 2021.

pmc-11299394.title: A living experience proposal for the co-occurring diagnosis of avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder and other eating disorders
pmc-11299394.creator: Sam L Sharpe
pmc-11299394.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The eating and feeding disorder section of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders 5 Text Revision (DSM-5-TR) is organized by a diagnostic algorithm that limits the contemporaneous assignment of multiple eating disorder diagnoses. Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) is a disturbance in food intake typically associated with lack of interest in food, food avoidance based on sensory characteristics, and/or fear of aversive consequences from eating.

pmc-11433965.title: Contact Hole Shrinkage: Simulation Study of Resist Flow Process and Its Application to Block Copolymers
pmc-11433965.creator: Sang-Kon Kim
pmc-11433965.description: For vertical interconnect access (VIA) in three-dimensional (3D) structure chips, including those with high bandwidth memory (HBM), shrinking contact holes (C/Hs) using the resist flow process (RFP) represents the most promising technology for low-k1 (where CD=k1λ/NA, CD is the critical dimension, λ is wavelength, and NA is the numerical aperture).

pmc-11574211.title: Three-year changes in high-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T and total mortality in older adults
pmc-11574211.creator: Dhayana Dallmeier, Johanna Braisch, Michael Denkinger, Wolfgang Koenig, Dietrich Rothenbacher
pmc-11574211.description: Elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T (hs-cTnT) is associated with mortality in older adults. However, little is known about the implications of changes over time. We investigated hs-cTnT 3-year change and its association with subsequent mortality in the Activity and Function in the Elderly Study. Participants with baseline and follow-up hs-cTnT < 5 ng/L built the reference group (G1 = 156).

pmc-12412138.title: Descriptive Analysis and Factors Associated With Relapse in Dogs With Presumptive Idiopathic Immune‐Mediated Polyarthritis
pmc-12412138.creator: Diane Pichard, Thibaud Robin, Kevin Le Boedec, Christelle Maurey, Maxime Kurtz, Fiona Da Riz, Stéphane Blot, Morgane Canonne‐Guibert, Mario Cervone, Emilie Krafft, Jean‐Luc Cadore, Loïc Desquilbet, Ghita Benchekroun
pmc-12412138.description: BackgroundImmune‐mediated polyarthritis (IMPA) is a joint disease common in dogs. Although its prognosis is generally favorable, relapses are frequent, and predictive factors for relapse remain poorly characterized.ObjectivesTo evaluate the outcome of medical management of IMPA in dogs and identify predictive factors for relapse.AnimalsClient‐owned dogs diagnosed with non‐associative IMPA between 2010 and 2022 across four veterinary referral centers.

pmc-12474589.title: A solitary ulcer on the tongue
pmc-12474589.creator: Annalina Meyka, Eva Schadelbauer, Birger Kränke, Birgit Sadoghi
pmc-12474589.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Syphilis is a systemic sexually transmitted infection caused by the invasive bacterium Treponema pallidum. The diagnosis remains challenging since the disease is labeled as “the great imitator” due to its broad clinical and histopathological appearances. Due to a significant rise in its incidence rates, syphilis should always be considered as a differential diagnosis of any painless, newly developed, oropharyngeal ulcerated lesion. This case demonstrates the rare clinical appearance of a chancre on the tongue as the primary clinical sign of syphilis.

pmc-12590724.title: Association of periodontal disease with risk atrial fibrillation: systematic review
pmc-12590724.creator: Luo Xin-nian, Luo Xin-yi
pmc-12590724.description: BackgroundPeriodontal disease (PD), a chronic inflammatory condition affecting nearly 50% of adults globally, drives systemic inflammation and cardiovascular diseases. Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia, shares pathophysiological links with inflammation. This systematic review evaluates the association between PD and AF risk, addressing gaps in existing evidence.

pmc-12606627.title: The Effects of Chirality and Salt Addition on Phase Separation and Complexation Morphology in Mixtures of Polypeptides and Polypeptoids
pmc-12606627.creator: Kimiasadat Mirlohi, Anuja Thapa, Donghui Zhang, Whitney C. Blocher McTigue
pmc-12606627.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), particularly through coacervation, offers a groundbreaking approach to drug delivery by encapsulating therapeutic agents within phase-separated droplets, enhancing their stability, solubility, and controlled release. Polypeptides and polypeptoids, with their structural diversity and tunability, emerge as promising candidates for exploring these systems, with polypeptoids offering unique advantages, such as resistance to enzymatic degradation and increased control over interactions.

pmc-12805736.title: S1PR3 Inhibition in alveolar epithelial cells alleviates pulmonary fibrosis by enhancing alveolar barrier function
pmc-12805736.creator: Mengyao Hao, Guodong Tang, Enjia Zhou, Rong Fu, MingJin Wang, Huimin Jiang, Xiaoguang Chen, Liping Bai, Xiaoxi Lv, Jing Jin
pmc-12805736.description: BackgroundPulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a chronic and progressive respiratory disease characterized by the destruction of the alveolar–capillary barrier. Repeated injury and abnormal repair of alveolar epithelial cells lead to barrier dysfunction and fibroblast activation. The sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor (S1PR) signaling pathways are critical for regulating physiological barrier function.

pmc-13134972.title: The Formula of Humanity and AI Use
pmc-13134972.creator: Martin Sticker
pmc-13134972.description: Aylsworth and Castro have argued that, following Kant’s Formula of Humanity, using ChatGPT to write humanities essays constitutes a violation of a duty to cultivate one’s humanity. I first turn to a critical evaluation of their argument and then point to a further dimension in which the FH has a bearing on the ethics of AI use.

pmc-13326519.title: Cross‐stage single‐cell and spatial metabolome analyses reveal periderm specialization and tanshinone biosynthesis in Salvia miltiorrhiza roots
pmc-13326519.creator: Licheng Liu, Lianchong Gao, Zhi‐Ying Wang, Yan Liu, Huifeng Ju, Huana Lin, Zheng Shi, Wen‐Juan Cai, Xue Li, Yan‐Bo Huang, Yu Kong, Jing‐Jing Xu, Hong‐Peng Chen, Xin Fang, Juan Guo, Yong‐Hong Hu, Ke Chen, Xiao‐Ya Chen, Jie Hao, Lei Yang
pmc-13326519.description: Summary Perennial herbs develop long‐lived roots that undergo repeated cycles of secondary growth, during which the periderm functions as a protective barrier and a major site of specialized metabolite accumulation. However, the cellular programs that coordinate periderm differentiation and secondary metabolism in perennial roots remain poorly understood.

pmc-13501086.title: Shift Angle and Medial Retraction of the Deep Layer on Magnetic Resonance Imaging Are Associated With Intraoperative Reparability in Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair
pmc-13501086.creator: Hideya Yoshimura, Hiroko Ueki, Naoko Araya
pmc-13501086.description: PurposeTo determine whether magnetic resonance imaging‐based measurements of the deep layer, specifically the shift angle and medial retraction, can predict intraoperative reparability of large‐to‐massive rotator cuff tears.MethodsThis retrospective study included patients who underwent arthroscopic repair of large‐to‐massive rotator cuff tears between April 2015 and September 2019, with a minimum follow‐up of 12 months.
